question: Does the transformer/MLP blend beat same-cost two-model averages of a single family?
disclosure: post hoc control on already-scored holdout test predictions; blend result known; no model trained or reselected

controls.transformer_pair: equal average of zero-clipped transformer seeds s and next(s)

pairing: seed slot 401 uses 401+402, 402 uses 402+403, 403 uses 403+401 (cyclic, fixed); blend slot s uses transformer s + MLP s with its locked alpha
weights: fixed 0.5 for same-family pairs (symmetric seeds); blend keeps its locked validation alpha
recordings: set B D3,D4,D7,D9 for the decision; TX60_s2 descriptive
decision: claim that mixing architectures adds beyond same-cost averaging only if the blend beats EACH control with mean relative MSE gain>0, >=3/4 mouse wins and >=8/12 seed-slot wins; otherwise conclude averaging explains the benefit
